summary: The test suite provides good coverage of core retention policy logic (age, size, keep-latest-N, dry-run) and includes clear Pester patterns with mocking. However, it critically fails the explicit requirement that 'ALL TESTS MUST RUN THROUGH ACT': the tests run directly with Invoke-Pester, not through the GitHub Actions workflow in an isolated Docker container. The task mandates a test harness that sets up git repos, runs `act push` per test case, captures output to `act-result.txt`, and asserts on exact expected values—none of this is present. Workflow structure validation is superficial (file existence, actionlint syntax); no tests verify the workflow actually executes successfully. Fixture files are referenced but not shown in the submission, making full evaluation impossible. Edge cases are incomplete (zero/negative size boundaries, artifact tie-breaking, deletion failure handling). The core module logic would likely be regression-safe, but end-to-end system testing is absent.
